rv.q: “The Writer” is a very interesting and gutsy show.
This show is truly unexpected and thought-provoking!
I totally loved this production and this play.
The Writer by Ella Hickson, now in its U.S. premiere at Steep Theatre under the sure direction of Georgette Verdin, is a maddening yet compelling exploration of art, power, commerce, and gender.
But The Writer needs some work to get a little closer to being, if not a “Good Play, then at least a story well told.
The production itself is quite solid, but fatally compromised by a script that either doesn’t know what it wants to say, or is afraid to say it without equivocation.
It’s a feminist manifesto with choreography.

cn.t: This meta-theatrical exploration of gender and power in theatre divides critics with its self-conscious structure and unwinnable arguments, earning praise for its incisive ideas but frustration for its messy execution.
